Ikhwezi Lokusa

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
In 2018 we did two stories on Ikwezi Lokusa, where the department made us numerous promises of education about improvements at the school. Still, five years later, the school has become less safe for the children rather than seeing any gains.

According to the teaching staff on sight – who will speak anonymously – there is a severe lack of care staff. I must confirm what the current ratio is, but there is a mandated ratio that they are supposed to have. Due to a lack of careers, the most vulnerable of disabled children are being left alone for hours on end, during shift changes and on weekends. The children’s nappies are not being changed, and the children themselves are filthy.
No social workers, physiotherapists, or occupational therapists are employed at the school; again, they are mandated to have a quota for all the above.

Before our story started, Mveli Siyabulela was employed as support staff at the school in 2016; he was dismissed due to rape allegations. He was then rehired, and in June this year took a CP boy off-site on Saturday morning and only returned him on Sunday. He has been arrested and charged with rape. He is currently awaiting trial.

These disabled children, from families with nowhere else, to send them, are being forgotten by the government and left to suffer.

Establish the school.
Writing on the screen - Ikwezi Lokusa Special School
Mthatha

GOV: Principle, can I speak to you, please - under the school vis.
GOV: Principle, please, before you go into class
Principle: I am busy
GOV: Principle, please, it’s about the children being left alone
Principle: I don’t want to answer you

A special needs school where the very people supposed to protect and care for these children are the ones abusing and neglecting them. This is an investigation that delivers one shocking truth after another.

DOE:
Let me take the fall on that one and see probably, as the department we failed on that one. On rotating him.
G:
Because he's an accused paedophile, that's what he is.

Or

He asked him to come with him as he would return to school later that day for his shift
They went to his house, and that's where he tried to rape him


Fade to black
Fade up from black.

We first investigated Ikwezi Lokusa, a government special needs boarding school in Mthatha, in the Eastern Cape 5 years ago.
And we were horrified by what we found, Children being forced to sleep on brick beds. It wasn’t a safe place for any child, let alone one with special needs.

Claire in the bathroom: How are you supposed to grow a childs self-esteem and give them dignity in a place like this


One night, we found three women caring for nearly forty children.

NIGHT SCENE of women trying to clean the children
Housemother:

Believing the Department of Education was failing the children and desperate for change, the principal at the time, Archie Galwa, gave us full access to the school.

Ep 1
00:12:36 Claire and Archie Claire: if you had a child with CP, would you be happy that they came and attended this school
Archie: I would opt for another institution
Claire: that’s heartbreaking
Archie: yeah, but that’s the truth


In this 2018 interview, the Eastern Cape Department of Education committed to solving the crisis at Ikwezi Lokusa.






EP 1
00:06:00
Sharon:
This year we have put 150 non-teaching staff out to improve the situation
Claire: But can you put a timeline to that
Sharon: They will be in place before next the next.


“Next year” was 2019, but it came and went without the department delivering on its promise.

LINK: GOVAN
A few weeks ago, we got a tip off saying that the conditions at Ikhwesi Lokusa were worse than anything we saw in 2018. So, we returned. But this time they refused to allow us to film.

PRINCIPLES ASSISTANT:
They said you must wait in the office
But you can go around if you stay next to the pool

Allowed into the boarding houses, our crew captured what they could on their cell phones.


HOUSEMOTHER: no curtain and no heating

It’s clear things have deteriorated since 2018: no improvements have been made to the children's sleeping space; the stench of urine hangs in the air of the filthy dormitories.

G: You know, I’ve been on a lot of prison raids
The conditions in prison are much better

There’ve been no renovations in the bathrooms either, which remain a health hazard. When we visited, there was no running water in any of the dormitories.

Anon teacher
The structure is no longer conducive for the disabled learners.
In fact, it’s an old building, so it needs to be renovated.


Ziyanda - which isn’t her real name – has been a teacher at Ikhwesi Lokusa for more than a decade. Desperate to help the children, she agreed to speak to us.

The kids are sad. They cry and want to go home.

Ikwezi Lokusa, meaning the “The Morning Star” in isiXhosa, was built by missionary sisters in 1965. It was a state-of-the-art facility, a beacon of hope for disabled children in the former Transkei.
In 2005 government took over the school, renting the property from the church.

Yo, yes Ikwezi Lokusa used to be a good school.

Everywhere are signs of the school’s former glory: the home economics classrooms now permanently locked, the rehabilitation pools empty of water, the derelict physiotherapy room




Teacher:
It is sad, they cannot renovate the school as it belongs to the nuns not the government.



In each dormitory, 3 or 4 caregivers working 8-hour shifts look after around 20 children.
The day shift ends at three in the afternoon and the night shift starts at six. We were told casual staff care for the children when they are not on duty

Visual:: Us walking into the room

But when we checked, we found the children on their own.

Visual: walking in and the kids going crazy
Kids everywhere


This little girl was being bathed in cold water by her friends.
These two had lifted themselves out of their wheelchairs and onto the broken toilet seats. Most shocking, though, was the sight of this young girl trying to change her own nappy in a darkened corner of the bathroom.

TARRYn: my god
TARRYN: I’m going to get somebody

Our producer searched for help, eventually finding the housemother in charge of these girls who’re aged between 6 and 12.

HMOTHER: I am only supposed to be here at 6’oclock, there are 4 of us
PRODUCER: So who is supposed to be here
HMOTHER: The aunties
PRODUCER: Where are they
HMOTHER: I don’t go. GO AND ASK THE SUPERVISOR. THERE IS A SUPERVISOR HERE

Adaman it wasn’t her problem, we went in search of the supervisor, eventually finding her on a break in her car.

Producer: No one is looking after the children.
SUPERVISOR: Where are the aunties (casual workers)?
producer: There is no one there. There has been no one there
S: They are coming
You are not going to change us. You are here working for Carte Blanche, we are going there. We are supervisors, and we are on lunch and waiting for the aunties who will be in at 6pm.

We went back to the girl's dormitory followed slowly by the rest of the caregiver.

What we saw was almost too grotesque to film.

Beat from the scene - kids screaming.

Vulnerable, mentally and physically disabled children dragged themselves naked across cold cement floors. The children weren’t being bathed; simply wiped down with a cold rag and moved aside.

These were children… taking care of children

ANON TEACHER:
Yo, It’s very, it’s very heartbreaking, because when you see that these kids need to be cared for.
When the kids smell bad, you think, who was supposed to clean these children?

The children no longer have dignity now, when you look at them you feel sorry for them

Later, the children were put to bed in a communal living space without underwear on.

ANON TEACHER
The aunties don't put panties on them because they don't want to wash those panties..

GOVAN: I knew this place was going to be bad, but what Ive seen here tonight has completely shattered me

Walking down the passage at night:
Haunted by what we’d seen we left later that night, promising to return in the morning.
Fade to black
Fade up

Visual: Headlights driving onto the school, past the sign

We arrived at 6 just as the night shift was ending, driving onto the property without anyone so much as asking our names.

Car door opens, feet out and walks into the school
Into the girls dorm.
producer: “no - one is here”
producer: “Where is u mumma”
Kids: “She is gone”

The caregivers were nowhere to be seen, leaving 20 young disabled girls between 6 and 12 without adult supervision.

Visual of us walking through the school

Making our way from dormitory to dormitory, we realised there wasn’t a single adult on the campus looking after close to 200 children with special needs.

Upsound beat
Gov walking

More than an hour passed before the first members of staff started arriving. With serious questions needing answers, we went in search of the school's principal.

GOVAN: Sorry, principal, please can I speak to you
GOVAN: Principle, please
PRINCIPLE: I do not want to answer you. Do you want to make me cry
GOVAN: We need to know why the children are being left alone
PRINCIPLE:
GOVAN: About being left alone
PRINCIPLE: I do not own this school. The school belongs to the DOE

The principal was adamant that responsibility for the failings at Ikwezi Lokusa lay with the Eastern Cape Department of Education.

GOVAN: Principle, why will you not answer for the children they are living in conditions that are not tolerable
GOVAN: Why are you, principle why are you running away from us?

GOVAN: link to camera
She is more concerned about what the department thinks of her than state of the school and the fact that these kids are being left alone

Visual: car driving into the village
Govan gets out

Tragically, that wasn’t the worst our investigation would uncover. We learnt that a 16-year-old boy with cerebral palsy – a condition that effects a childs ability to move, and their cognitive functioning - accused his housefather of sexual assault in June this year.

Beat pause

We tracked down his mother a two-hour drive from Mthatha in a remote area of the province.


NOBALEKO
It was a rainy day around 26 May when they met on Facebook,. He then called him to come to the gate at the back.
He asked him to come with him as he would return to school later that day for his shift
They went to his house, and that's where he tried to rape him

It’s claimed the housefather took the boy to his flat on a Saturday morning, returning him to the school only the following night. The boys mother says not one of Ikhwezi Lokusa’s staff members noticed her son was missing.

I don’t feel well ever since this happened to my child he is depressed. He even said to his sister that it would be better if he committed suicide.

The housefather has been arrested and is awaiting trial, but the childs family have been forced to leave their traumatised son at Ikwezi Lokusa, because it is the only government special needs boarding school servicing this remote area of the former Transkei

There is nothing I would love to say except pleading with the government to add security at that school, there is nothing else I can say.


Then, moments before we leave, the boys mother reveals that the house father …. may have assaulted another boy, close to 10 years ago.

To get answers, we traced Archie Gulwa, the school's principal at that time.

ARCHIE INTERVIEW IN THE CAR
Hi, it's Govan Whittles. Yeah, I'm calling from Carte Blanche. You remember us? Yes

Alarmingly, Archie confirmed the very same housefather accused of rape this year, was alleged to have done the same in 2014.

taking his victim out of the hostel at night and returning him in the morning


G: Why did this guy get away with this?
they stated at the court of law that there was no evidence on the side of the kids.

No evidence to prove that he did this.
Was the victim able to speak clearly
No not at all

According to Archie the child had cerebral palsy and could not provide clear testimony, so the charges were dropped.
The housefather was immediately reinstated at Ikwhesi Lokusa by the Department of Education.

A: The boy was very much upset, and not at ease at all so we decided to transfer him to another school.
G: So instead of moving the housefather, you move the learner.
A: Yeah, since the Department of Education never helped us to take the guy away from the learner.

It was time to confront the Eastern Cape Department of Education. IN East London, we met the Director of Inclusive Education, simone Ncapayi


G: I'm sure the department is aware of the housefather who is currently behind bars for having sexually assaulted a learner.
DOE: We are aware, and while he is behind bars we have already served him with the letter of suspension. Even if he can get bail today, he's not going to go back to school.

G: So, were you aware that he had previously faced a charge of sexual assault years ago at the same school?
DOE:
We are aware that in 2014, the very same men there was this accusation.
G:
But he was sent back to work at the same school with the same learners from 2016 to 2023.
DOE:
Let me take the fall on that one and say the department we failed on that one. On rotating him.
G:
Because he's an accused paedophile, that's what he is.
Mr.. MACAPAYI do you honestly believe that between 2016 and 2023 he did nothing to any of the other boys?

DOE:
I cannot stand here and say I believe that these are the only two cases. And it's unfortunate.
G
It's a travesty.
DOE
More than a travesty.

When confronted with footage of the children’s inhumane living conditions, Macapayi said the church, from which the Department was only renting the property, had failed to maintain the school.

Its a public school on a private property, but becasue those learners are ours so we. can’t allow them to stay on a property

After more than a decade, they are now committing to revamping Ikwhesi lokusa

DOE: We have assessed the whole school. We are busy costing it. We cannot allow our children to go in these beds. The demolition of those beds will be finalised and finished by December.
G: Thank you for updating us on the plans of the department
G: Was the department aware that the children are being left alone for more than an hour at a time?
G: No, we are not aware, as that school should not be having those problems

With 65 care workers, Ikwesi Lokusa is fully staffed, which begs the question, why are these children still being neglected?

G: What responsibility is it to ensure that the children are not been left alone?

DOE: I want to say that the principal should be the one who is ensuring that workers are divided across the school

G: So the principal wasn't doing the job. and the department didn't know. Let's look at how they're living, sir. Look at these videos of what we saw there. If you can see here, this is the children being left alone inside the facility
There's no caregiver.

DOE: Then who gave you access there?

G: Are you concerned about the condition of the children or the fact that we have these videos?

DOE: I am concerned about both

G: These children are crawling around naked inside the facility at night. They are being forced to sleep naked because no one is washing the panties of the children. It reeks of urine. What do you have to say about all of this?

DOE: Hence I'm saying to you, FOR me, this is very unfortunate.

G: I want to clarify that our reason for being here is not to tell a news story. We are here to ensure that a change happens at Ikwhesi Lokusal. So what can the department promise today that will be done at that school?

DOE: It's very easy because we will go to Ikwhesi Lokusa so that we deal with each individual who is supposed to be dealing with dilemmas because they are conscious. Are they doing that to their kids in their own homes? There's no way that we can allow such a situation.

With yet more promised from the Department of Education, we’ll be back for a third time to ensure that these children get the treatment and care they deserve.

He asked him to come with him as he would return to school later that day for his shift They went to his house, and that's where he tried to rape him It’s claimed the housefather took the boy to his flat on a Saturday morning, returning him to the school only the following night. The boys mother says not one of Ikhwezi Lokusa’s staff members noticed her son was missing. I don’t feel well ever since this happened to my child he is depressed. He even said to his sister that it would be better if he committed suicide. The housefather has been arrested and is awaiting trial, but the childs family have been forced to leave their traumatised son at Ikwezi Lokusa, because it is the only government special needs boarding school servicing this remote area of the former Transkei There is nothing I would love to say except pleading with the government to add security at that school, there is nothing else I can say. Then, moments before we leave, the boys mother reveals that the house father …. may have assaulted another boy, close to 10 years ago. To get answers, we traced Archie Gulwa, the school's principal at that time. ARCHIE INTERVIEW IN THE CAR Hi, it's Govan Whittles. Yeah, I'm calling from Carte Blanche. You remember us? Yes Alarmingly, Archie confirmed the very same housefather accused of rape this year, was alleged to have done the same in 2014. taking his victim out of the hostel at night and returning him in the morning G: Why did this guy get away with this? they stated at the court of law that there was no evidence on the side of the kids. No evidence to prove that he did this. Was the victim able to speak clearly No not at all According to Archie the child had cerebral palsy and could not provide clear testimony, so the charges were dropped. The housefather was immediately reinstated at Ikwhesi Lokusa by the Department of Education. A: The boy was very much upset, and not at ease at all so we decided to transfer him to another school. G: So instead of moving the housefather, you move the learner. A: Yeah, since the Department of Education never helped us to take the guy away from the learner. It was time to confront the Eastern Cape Department of Education. IN East London, we met the Director of Inclusive Education, simone Ncapayi G: I'm sure the department is aware of the housefather who is currently behind bars for having sexually assaulted a learner. DOE: We are aware, and while he is behind bars we have already served him with the letter of suspension. Even if he can get bail today, he's not going to go back to school. G: So, were you aware that he had previously faced a charge of sexual assault years ago at the same school? DOE: We are aware that in 2014, the very same men there was this accusation. G: But he was sent back to work at the same school with the same learners from 2016 to 2023. DOE: Let me take the fall on that one and say the department we failed on that one. On rotating him. G: Because he's an accused paedophile, that's what he is. Mr.. MACAPAYI do you honestly believe that between 2016 and 2023 he did nothing to any of the other boys? DOE: I cannot stand here and say I believe that these are the only two cases. And it's unfortunate. G It's a travesty. DOE More than a travesty. When confronted with footage of the children’s inhumane living conditions, Macapayi said the church, from which the Department was only renting the property, had failed to maintain the school. Its a public school on a private property, but becasue those learners are ours so we. can’t allow them to stay on a property After more than a decade, they are now committing to revamping Ikwhesi lokusa DOE: We have assessed the whole school. We are busy costing it. We cannot allow our children to go in these beds. The demolition of those beds will be finalised and finished by December. G: Thank you for updating us on the plans of the department G: Was the department aware that the children are being left alone for more than an hour at a time? G: No, we are not aware, as that school should not be having those problems With 65 care workers, Ikwesi Lokusa is fully staffed, which begs the question, why are these children still being neglected? G: What responsibility is it to ensure that the children are not been left alone? DOE: I want to say that the principal should be the one who is ensuring that workers are divided across the school G: So the principal wasn't doing the job. and the department didn't know. Let's look at how they're living, sir. Look at these videos of what we saw there. If you can see here, this is the children being left alone inside the facility There's no caregiver. DOE: Then who gave you access there? G: Are you concerned about the condition of the children or the fact that we have these videos? DOE: I am concerned about both G: These children are crawling around naked inside the facility at night. They are being forced to sleep naked because no one is washing the panties of the children. It reeks of urine. What do you have to say about all of this? DOE: Hence I'm saying to you, FOR me, this is very unfortunate. G: I want to clarify that our reason for being here is not to tell a news story. We are here to ensure that a change happens at Ikwhesi Lokusal. So what can the department promise today that will be done at that school? DOE: It's very easy because we will go to Ikwhesi Lokusa so that we deal with each individual who is supposed to be dealing with dilemmas because they are conscious. Are they doing that to their kids in their own homes? There's no way that we can allow such a situation. With yet more promised from the Department of Education, we’ll be back for a third time to ensure that these children get the treatment and care they deserve.

metadata.Summary: In 2018 we did two stories on Ikwezi Lokusa, where the department made us numerous promises of education about improvements at the school. Still, five years later, the school has become less safe for the children rather than seeing any gains. According to the teaching staff on sight – who will speak anonymously – there is a severe lack of care staff. I must confirm what the current ratio is, but there is a mandated ratio that they are supposed to have. Due to a lack of careers, the most vulnerable of disabled children are being left alone for hours on end, during shift changes and on weekends. The children’s nappies are not being changed, and the children themselves are filthy. No social workers, physiotherapists, or occupational therapists are employed at the school; again, they are mandated to have a quota for all the above. Before our story started, Mveli Siyabulela was employed as support staff at the school in 2016; he was dismissed due to rape allegations. He was then rehired, and in June this year took a CP boy off-site on Saturday morning and only returned him on Sunday. He has been arrested and charged with rape. He is currently awaiting trial. These disabled children, from families with nowhere else, to send them, are being forgotten by the government and left to suffer.
